newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said five percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was harvested compared with 15 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 11 percent.

In the report on conditions for the week ended June 15, USDA said three percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, nine percent poor, 27 percent fair, 51 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
The department said one percent of the U.S. corn crop was in very poor condition, five percent poor, 28 percent fair, 54 percent good and 12 percent excellent.
It said 89 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was planted compared with 70 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 80 percent.
The department reported two percent of the U.S. cotton crop was in very poor condition, nine percent poor, 29 percent fair, 50 percent good and 10 percent excellent.

USDA said 97 percent of the U.S. spring wheat crop had emerged compared with 92 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 96 percent. Fifty-nine percent of the crop was in good-to-excellent condition compared with 74 percent a year ago, the department said.
